html:
SMTO-LLM-0062 — Model not found

GUID: d7d3b3ae-59bb-5cd7-96a7-48777ec9481f
Slug: local-ai-model-not-found
Domain: LLM · Subsystem: local_ai

What happened

  • The model file or folder named in your model server profile isn't at that location on the Gateway's computer, so the model server wasn't started.

How to fix — simple steps

  1. On the Gateway's computer, find where the model is saved and copy its full location, starting with / (for llama.cpp, the model file itself, not its folder). SMTO needs the exact full location on that computer; a copy elsewhere doesn't count.
  2. Open Parameter Store, select the Local AI Runtime profile, put that location in model_path, and select Save. The model server is started with whatever location the profile gives.
  3. Ask SMTO to show the Local AI status for that Gateway, the helper program SMTO uses on that computer, and check whether a model server from earlier is already running. Starting again while an earlier copy is still running could create a second copy.
  4. Start the model server again in a new message that names the profile with @ (use Copy reference in Parameter Store). A task keeps the profile it started with, so only a new message picks up your saved changes.

What success looks like

  • The model server starts and its status shows ready.

If it still fails

  • Select Copy error details and send them to the person who manages that Gateway; the model may be only partly copied or in a folder the Gateway can't read.

Technical details

Observed condition

  • The profile's model_path is not an existing absolute path on the selected Gateway (and, for llama.cpp, not a regular file), so the launch plan was rejected before any process was created.

What this means

  • The launch adapter requires an existing absolute model path and, for llama.cpp, a regular file; the selected path does not meet that requirement. Local AI management belongs to the selected Gateway and accepted profile. Starting a runtime does not activate it for the controller; recorded execution and unknown-effect facts determine whether reconciliation is required.

Why this can happen

  • The launch adapter requires an existing absolute model path and, for llama.cpp, a regular file; the selected path does not meet that requirement.

How to diagnose it

  • Inspect the model path on the selected Gateway and distinguish a missing path, relative path and wrong file type.

How to fix it

  • On the Gateway host, confirm model_path is absolute and exists for the Gateway service account (llama.cpp needs the model file itself, such as a .gguf; vLLM accepts a model directory). Copy the complete model there or correct model_path in the Local AI Runtime Parameter, then start a new task with the updated revision.
  • Stage the intended complete model artifact on the Gateway and update the accepted profile path.

Retry and execution caution

  • Only after exact state reconciliation.

How to verify the fix

  • The profile names an existing absolute model artifact of the type required by its provider.

What not to do

  • Do not replay uncertain mutations or stop externally owned processes.

Technical notes

  • Local AI management belongs to the selected Gateway and accepted profile. Starting a runtime does not activate it for the controller; recorded execution and unknown-effect facts determine whether reconciliation is required.
  • Preserve the occurrence ID and safe request/operation references. Receipts and occurrence facts establish what started or completed; the catalog does not authorize retries or establish execution outcome.
